THE GENERAL SITUATION IN KWANGTUNG.

The year 1923 has not been a happy one for the Province
of Kwangtung. Sun Yat Sen's Government, although much feted
by the syndicalists and Cantonese labourers, lost during the
year a great deal of the sympathy which it had acquired through
supporting the strike movements and openly helping the movements
of the labourers in their struggle against the employer.
The golden age promised by the socialist leaders in the
pay of Sun Yat Sen has not yet arrived. The distress of the
people has been greater than it has ever been. The country-side
pillaged by the troops in Kwangtung have been deserted by the
farmers. Canton abounds with miserable people, with women and
children who are half clad and who are demanding charity, and
who are even disputing with the dogs in the streets over the
rubbish heaps for the food which they can rake out of them.
The incessant warfare between Sun Yat Sen and Chen Chuin
Ming in the suburbs of Canton with varying fortunes of war, has
ruined this rich province. The whole population has been affected.
And if during the first few months of the year the syndicalists
were rejoicing over the oppression and the robbery of the
merchants and the employers, they had to regret it. Abandoned
by their employers, they were left alone to fight against the
activities of the indisciplined soldiers who regarded the city
as conquered territory.
To maintain these mercenary troops money was required.
Now it was difficult to raise money as all revenue had passed
into the hands of these transient allies. The large companies
of Yunnanese troops of Yang Hi Ming, the hordes of Kwangsi men
of Lieou, those also of Hunan and the Cantonese constitutional
troops, --all these formed a confused band of brigands of the
first order. They rivalled each other in attempting to obtain
as much as possible from a Government whose treasury is always
empty and which had succeeded in raising money by means of
shameful extortion in order that its followers may not turn
against it. It has been thus for several months, and during
these months the Generalissimo found new expedients. But he
never neglected to set aside important reserves which would
assure a future of plenty. Merchants, industrialists and workers
had to contribute, voluntarily or by force, the major part of
their income. The landlords, although they paid all the taxes,
had not touched a cent of their rentals for the past four months.
The Canton Municipality, under the high direction of Sun Fo,
the Mayor, and son of Sun Yat Sen, saved the landlords the
trouble of banking their income from their real estate, the
Municipality undertaking this work for them. Thus Sun Yat Sen
and his collaborators were able to live a merry life.

广东的总体局势。

1923年对广东省而言并非幸运之年。孙中山政府虽然受到工团主义者和广东劳工的大肆吹捧，但在这一年里，它因支持罢工运动并公开帮助劳工在与雇主的斗争中对抗雇主而获得的同情心丧失殆尽。受雇于孙中山的社会党领袖们所许诺的黄金时代尚未到来。民众的困苦比以往任何时候都更为深重。广东军队洗劫过的乡村已被农民抛弃。广州城里到处都是悲惨的人，衣不蔽体的妇女和儿童乞求施舍，甚至与街上的狗争夺垃圾堆里能刨出的食物。孙中山与陈炯明在广州郊区的战事连绵不断，胜负交替，使这个富庶的省份沦为废墟。全体居民均受波及。如果在年初的几个月里，工团主义者还在为商人和雇主遭受的压迫与抢劫而欢欣鼓舞，那么他们随后便不得不为此感到后悔。被雇主抛弃后，他们只能独自面对那些视城市为征服地的纪律涣散士兵的活动。

为了维持这些雇佣军，需要资金。然而，由于所有收入都落入了这些 transient allies（临时盟友）的手中，筹款变得十分困难。杨希闵（Yang Hi Ming）的大批滇军、刘氏（Lieou）的广西人团伙，以及湖南部队和广东宪政军——所有这些构成了一群第一流的乌合之众般的匪徒。他们竞相从一个国库始终空虚的政府那里尽可能多地榨取钱财，而该政府为了使其追随者不倒戈，竟通过可耻的勒索手段成功筹集资金。这种情况持续了数月，在这几个月里，大元帅找到了新的权宜之计。但他从未忘记留出重要的储备金，以确保未来的富足。商人、工业家和工人被迫自愿或强制地贡献出其收入的大部分。地主虽然缴纳了所有税款，但在过去四个月里未收到分文租金。在市长兼孙中山之子孙科的高层指导下，广州市政府免去了地主存储房地产收入的麻烦，由市政府代为处理此项工作。因此，孙中山及其同伙得以过着快乐的生活。

It is possible to find a number of minor officials at
the offices between 10 a.m. and noon, but the head of
departments are conspicuous by their absence. They are working
off the effects of their gambling and indigestion of the night
before. It is not uncommon to find invoked as excuse for not
attending office the excuse of a series of feastings or other
similar ceremonies which would not allow them any time to
answer an urgent summons. Things can look after themselves.
In addition to a complete ignorance of their duties, the new
style officials of the Government are insolent and filthy
mouthed. All officers who have some standing and relative
value have to retire before the creatures of Sun Yat Sen.
Boys and coolies with a little qualification can hope to reach
the highest ranks in the army whose generals are former pirate
chiefs or become office employees, such as the general
commanding the Police On To Sin, who was formerly an employee
of a European commercial house in Shanghai. It is these people
who divide the town and who indulge in acts of piracy on the
river and on the Delta. To them everything is good.
If the landowners see themselves deprived of their real
estate, the labourers have also to pour out a good part of
their wages as contributions towards the numerous expeditions
against the north which resolve themselves into lectures on
the operations given at Sheilung and Waitcheou. It sometimes
happens that the plunderers come into disagreement, then the
inhabitants suffer, for the combatants will have recourse to
incendiarism and shots are fired.
To this one must add the recruiting of coolies and labourers
for the front, despite the protestations, the prayers and the
presents of the victims to the defenders of their liberty and
of the Constitution. The sweeps made daily in town have
terrorised the inhabitants who have never been noted for their
bravery, and it would be sufficient for a street-urchin to don
a military uniform to enable him to proceed with the recruiting
of five or six vigorous merry fellows. They have all been
paralysed with fear.
The sale of temples is regarded with disfavour by the
various corporations which had contributed towards their
purchase or their maintenance. Their protestations against had
no effect whatever upon the people who were selling the goods
of the ecclesiastics for their personal benefit. It is these
corporations only which have succeeded in preserving their
temples for they threatened to use force of arms. This was an
exceptional case.
The year 1923 could show no progress over the preceding
year in the labour question in Kwangtung Province. On the
other hand, there was a marked evolution towards communism
and Bolshevism. During the year, Sun Yat Sen's Government
gave irrefutable proofs of its incompetency to re-establish
order in a province which had suffered for many years from
the most complete anarchy. The Government had no money, the
schools were empty, administration was disorganized and trade
was paralyzed. The revenues of the province were seized by
the various Generals, chiefs of the bands holding Canton. The
authority of Sun Yat Sen extended to a distance of from 30 to
40 kilometres of the city; beyond that the troops and the
robbers were the masters.

(To be Continued).

上午10点至中午期间，可以在办公室里找到一些小官员，但各部门主管却不见踪影。他们正在缓解前一夜赌博和消化不良带来的影响。以一系列宴会或其他类似庆典活动为由，声称无暇回应紧急召唤，从而不出勤办公，这已屡见不鲜。事情可以自行解决。除了完全无视职责外，政府的新派官员还傲慢无礼、满口污言秽语。所有具有一定地位和相对价值的官员都必须在孙中山的亲信面前退位。稍有资历的童仆和苦力都有望跻身军队最高阶层，其将领多为前海盗头目；或者成为办公室职员，例如警察总监温宗尧（On To Sin），他曾是上海一家欧洲商行的雇员。正是这些人瓜分了城市，并在河流及三角洲地区从事海盗行径。对他们来说，一切手段都是可行的。

如果地主发现自己的不动产被剥夺，劳工也不得不拿出工资的一大部分，作为资助针对北方的众多远征军的捐款，而这些远征最终演变成在石龙（Sheilung）和惠州（Waitcheou）进行的作战行动讲解。掠夺者之间有时会发生分歧，此时居民便会遭殃，因为战斗人员会诉诸纵火并开枪射击。

此外，还必须加上在前线征募苦力和劳工的行为，尽管受害者向这些自由与宪法的捍卫者提出抗议、祈祷并献上礼物。每日在城内进行的搜捕行动吓坏了向来不以勇敢著称的居民，只要一个街头顽童穿上军装，就足以让他去征募五六个身强力壮的快乐小伙。所有人都因恐惧而瘫痪。

寺庙的出售遭到了曾出资购买或维护寺庙的各同业公会的反对。他们对那些为了个人利益出售教会财产的人提出的抗议毫无效果。只有这些公会成功保住了他们的寺庙，因为他们威胁要使用武力。这是一个特例。

1923年，广东省在劳工问题上相比前一年没有任何进展。另一方面，向共产主义和布尔什维主义发展的趋势明显。在这一年里，孙中山政府提供了无可辩驳的证据，证明其无力在一个多年来遭受完全无政府状态之苦的省份恢复秩序。政府没有资金，学校空无一人，行政混乱，贸易瘫痪。省财政收入被占据广州的各派系首领、将军们截留。孙中山的权威仅延伸至距城市30至40公里的范围内； beyond that（在此范围之外），军队和强盗才是主宰。

Translation from the Echo de Chine of April 8, 1924.

THE SOCIAL QUESTION IN KANTUNG DURING 1923.
(From the "Politique de Pekin.")
----------------------------------------
(Continued from yesterday).

LABOUR STRIKES.

The year 1923 was less prolific of bona fide labour strikes than 1922. The insecurity of the town for the unemployed largely contributed towards restraining labour movements. Better to work than to carry munitions or luggage of soldiers at the front to be paid with blows from the baton or from the butt-ends of rifles. The victims of forced military labour may be counted by the thousand, and many died of misery and of the ill-treatment to which they had to submit.
This provided food for reflection to the Cantonese labourers and calmed the ardour of the striker. Unfortunately for them the employers, oppressed by the local authorities, had to reduce the number of their employees. Furthermore, those institutions which depended upon the State had also to reduce their staffs because of lack of funds, and to pay them off with good words and fine promises. This was what happened to the Mint: one director was appointed after the other without being able to do anything, as there was no money to buy the materials. Financial institutions and private foreign and Chinese individuals were approached but nobody had any trust in the governmental concern, especially at a time when the leaders of the province were attempting to dispossess every body of his property. Sun Yat Sen was unable to obtain the two or three millions dollars required to set the Mint upon its feet. Nobody would believe in his promises and to the guarantees which he gave. Everybody saw that the security which he could put up had already been hypothecated to a Japanese bank. The swindler was thus baffled. In the meantime the labourers were waiting for the payment of their wages which were six months in arrears. Labour strikes were thus fewer when compared with the previous year, but those that took place extended over several months. All had for their object an increase of pay which the constantly going up of the high cost of living in Canton (the cost of living being very much higher than that in Shanghai and Hongkong) fully justified. But the employers, notwithstanding the fact that they often desired to do justice to the demands of the men, were not in a position to do so because they themselves were watched by the Police who employed the greater portion of their time in despoiling honest people.
The increases of pay ranged from 20% to 40%. The cost of manual labour became very high throughout the province and added considerably to the difficulties of the merchants. In a general way the labourers were satisfied with what they had gained in the course of the past year and which were: a general increase of wages, the last increase being insufficient this year owing to the anarchy and disorders which reigned throughout the province; an eight hour day, which has become the general rule; and the consecration of certain festivals as holidays for which the men are paid.
The public institutions and the Municipal service were particularly aimed at during the strikes of 1923. Short of funds, the staffs reduced and this led to strikes in sympathy (as in the case of the road sweepers and the drain workers). Short of money, wages were paid with nickel pieces which had no value, whilst the paper money was not even worth the paper.

译自1924年4月8日《中国回声报》（Echo de Chine）。

1923年广东的社会问题。
（摘自《北京政治》[Politique de Pekin]。）
----------------------------------------
（接昨日）。

劳工罢工。

1923年真正的劳工罢工次数少于1922年。城镇对失业者的不安全状况在很大程度上抑制了劳工运动。与其在前线搬运士兵的弹药或行李，挨棍棒或枪托的殴打，不如工作。被迫服军事劳役的受害者数以千计，许多人死于贫困和他们不得不忍受的虐待。

这给广东劳工带来了反思，并平息了罢工者的热情。不幸的是，受地方当局压迫的雇主不得不减少雇员数量。此外，那些依赖国家的机构也因缺乏资金而不得不裁员，并用好话和美好的承诺来打发他们。造币厂的情况便是如此：一任又一任厂长上任，却无所作为，因为没有钱购买材料。人们曾求助于金融机构以及私人的外国和中国个体，但没有人信任这家政府企业，尤其是在各省领导人试图剥夺每个人财产的时候。孙中山无法获得使造币厂运转所需的二三百万美元。没有人相信他的承诺和他提供的担保。每个人都看到，他能提供的抵押品已经抵押给了一家日本银行。这位骗子 thus（因此）受挫。与此同时，劳工们等待着支付已拖欠六个月的工资。因此，与前一年相比，罢工次数较少，但发生的罢工持续了数月。所有罢工的目的都是增加工资，广州生活成本的不断上涨（生活成本远高于上海和香港）充分证明了这一要求的合理性。但是，尽管雇主往往希望公正地对待工人的要求，但他们无力这样做，因为他们自己也受到警察的监视，而警察将大部分时间用于掠夺诚实的市民。

工资涨幅在20%到40%之间。全省体力劳动成本变得非常高，大大增加了商人的困难。总体而言，劳工们对过去一年所取得的成果感到满意，这些成果包括：普遍增加工资（由于全省盛行无政府状态和混乱，今年的最后一次增资显得不足）；八小时工作制已成为普遍规则；以及将某些节日定为带薪假期。

在1923年的罢工中，公共机构和市政服务特别成为目标。由于资金短缺，人员缩减，这导致了同情性罢工（如街道清扫工和下水道工人的情况）。由于缺钱，工资用没有价值的镍币支付，而纸币甚至还不如纸张值钱。

Silver money was scarce and there were in circulation many
counterfeit coins turned out by the Mint.
However, at the instigation of certain of the leaders
of the Kuomintang Party, certain Cantonese syndicates drew
up what they called the labour law of which the following
is a résumé:-

1) Recognition of the right of labourers to hold
public meetings, to organise unions and
associations.
2) The right to go on strike.
3) Recognition of the international unions of
labourers.
4) Day work of eight hours, night work of six hours,
with a maximum of 42 hours per week.
5) Working hours of children to be reduced to six,
working hours at heavy or unhealthy duties to
be reduced to six also.
6) Nobody may work a number of hours more than
the number fixed. However, in case of
necessity or urgency the hours may be extended
on the favourable advice of the syndicates.
7) Additional hours are to paid additional wages.
8) Women labourers will have the right to six
weeks holiday when they become pregnant.
9) The Government will fix the scale of wages after
securing the advice of the representatives of
the National Union of Labourers.
10) Labourers will have delegates in government
establishments as well as in private
establishments doing business for the State.
11) The Government will establish a special Labour
Bureau whose work will be to watch over the
protection o labourers.
12) Labourers must insure themselves against
accidents the premia being paid by the
Government or by the private establishments.
13) An annual holiday of one month for those who
have completed one year's service, and 15
days for those who have completed six months.
14) The Government will take all measures to
enable labourers to perfect their education.

Towards the end of this programme the following
four demands were added:-
1) Payment by the State of the cost of the education
of labourers.
2) Concession of 100 mows of public land on which
to construct a hospital for labourers.
3) Payment for Sundays.
4) Protection of labourers by Police and soldiers.

These new propositions were submitted by a small
number of labourers whose speciality is to promote meetings,
to form unions and to live at the expense of the real
sufferers..
By contrast, the political strikes were more serious
and grave. They were not at all similar to the strikes at
Hongkong and Macao in 1922, but were due to the policy of
Sun Yat Sen's Government.
In certain cases, it was the labourers who acted,
and in others, it was the employers themselves who went on
strike, and on many occasions the employers and the
labourers acted with one accord. All had the same purpose:
to resist the frequent demands of Sun Yat Sen for silver,
and to escape from the "squeeze" made by the officials in
the name of the Government.

银元稀缺，市面上流通着许多由造币厂出品的假币。
然而，在国民党某些领袖的煽动下，某些广东帮会起草了他们所谓的劳工法，其摘要如下：-

1) 承认劳动者举行公开集会、组织工会和协会的权利。
2) 罢工权。
3) 承认国际劳动者工会。
4) 白班工作八小时，夜班工作六小时，每周最多四十二小时。
5) 童工工作时间减至六小时，从事繁重或不健康工作的工时也减至六小时。
6) 任何人不得工作超过规定的小时数。但是，在必要或紧急情况下，经帮会从旁建议，可延长工作时间。
7) 加班时间须支付额外工资。
8) 女工怀孕时有权享受六周假期。
9) 政府在征求全国劳工联合会代表意见后，将确定工资标准。
10) 劳动者在政府机构以及为政府办理业务的私营机构中均应有代表。
11) 政府将设立一个专门的劳工局，其职责是监督对劳动者的保护。
12) 劳动者必须投保意外险，保费由政府或私营机构支付。
13) 服务满一年者享有一个月的年假，服务满六个月者享有十五天年假。
14) 政府将采取一切措施使劳动者能够完善其教育。

在该计划的末尾，又增加了以下四项要求：
1) 由国家支付劳动者的教育费用。
2) 拨给一百亩公地，用于建造一所劳工医院。
3) 支付星期日工资。
4) 由警察和士兵保护劳动者。

这些新主张是由少数劳动者提出的，他们的特长是促成集会、组建工会，并靠真正受苦者的血汗过活。
相比之下，政治性罢工更为严重和严峻。它们与1922年香港和澳门的罢工完全不同，而是源于孙中山政府的政策。
在某些情况下，是劳动者采取行动；而在其他情况下，则是雇主本人罢工；在许多场合，雇主和劳动者行动一致。所有各方都有相同的目的：抵制孙中山频繁索要银元的要求，并逃避官员以政府名义进行的“勒索”。

This resulted in several branches of commerce being almost
completely paralyzed and in the Government revoking the
orders or measures which had caused these manifestations.
The first strike was that of fire-works makers. It
was proposed to impose an additional tax on all orders as
well as on those which were about to be filled and delivered
at the time this new imposition was ordained. The reason
given for this additional tax was very simple: the Government
needed funds for its military operations, it was, therefore,
only right that every body should contribute. The makers
consequently decided to suspend their business, whilst the
labourers supported them in this action.
In the same an additional tax was imposed on tea shops.
But they all closed their doors. In both these cases the
Government has not revoked the measures taken. As regards
the fire-works makers, certain European firms who were
exporting fire-works to the United States were seriously
affected, and this brought forth protests from the Consuls
concerned.
The dock labourers and ship unloaders also went on strike
because the Government wanted to relieve them of a portion of
their wages. This strike has not yet ended, the labourers
refusing absolutely to submit to this taxation which would
reduce their income. Collisions have taken place between the
Police and the strikers, and following upon the killing of
one of the cargo unloaders the strike became complete so that
it was impossible to discharge steamers and vessels laden with
rice had to be sent to Hongkong with their cargoes. In the
meantime, the misery in Canton became aggravated. The
labourers, in claims against the government were supported by
the employers; in consequence, a number of yards had to close.
A strike of sampan men has also to be noted. This was
caused by the additional tax of 30 cents per day per sampan.
Two other important strikes have also to be recorded:
the rice and the silk strikes.
Sun Yat Sen's Government had on several occasions imposed
a tax on wholesale and retail rice dealers and to such a
degree that the imposts doubled the price of rice in Canton.
Furthermore, the Generalissimo attempted to revictual his
troops at the expense of the rice merchants. Soldiers were
posted at places where rice was to be discharged and they
seized what they required. In the face of such abuses, the
merchants decided not to import any more rice into Canton.
Local production being insufficient, it was feared that there
would be a shortage of the cereal. The leader of the strike
movement was assassinated with his wife and children.
The silk merchants were more heavily taxed. In this
instance there was complete harmony between the masters and the
men. Work was stopped purely and simply to await a settlement
of the dispute which had been submitted by the local Chamber
of Commerce to the Generalissimo.
The shawl makers had to submit to the taking of an
inventory of their stocks in the shops as prescribed by the
authorities. They had, in the majority of cases, taken
the necessary precautions and had arranged with the European
firms, who were their customers, to make disappear the larger
portion of their most important stocks. In order to protect
themselves against the visits of the Police, some of them
engaged Indian watchmen whose appearance alone was sufficient
to cause the investigators to keep at a distance.
Sun Yat Sen having declared that the official stamps on
invoices and other documents were not recognized in the free
Cantonese Republic, measures were taken by the authorities to
compel bankers and merchants (Chinese) to buy a supply of
southern stamps, which were only counterfeits of those
customarily used in other parts of China. The bankers
decided to close their doors if the measure was not
revoked. This threat had its effect and before long this

这导致几个商业部门几乎完全瘫痪，政府不得不撤销引发这些抗议活动的命令或措施。
第一次罢工是烟花爆竹制造者的罢工。当局提议对所有订单，包括在新征税令颁布时即将完成并交付的订单，征收附加税。征收此附加税的理由非常简单：政府需要资金用于军事行动，因此每个人都做出贡献是理所当然的。因此，制造商决定暂停营业，而劳动者则支持这一行动。
同样，茶馆也被征收附加税。但它们都关门停业。在这两个案例中，政府并未撤销所采取的措施。至于烟花爆竹制造商，某些向美国出口烟花的欧洲公司受到严重影响，这引起了相关领事馆的抗议。
码头工人和卸船工也举行了罢工，因为政府想要扣除他们部分工资。这次罢工尚未结束，劳动者绝对拒绝服从这种会降低其收入的征税。警察与罢工者之间发生了冲突，随着一名货物装卸工被杀，罢工变得彻底，导致无法卸载轮船，装载大米的船只不得不载着货物驶往香港。与此同时，广州的贫困状况加剧。劳动者在向政府提出诉求时得到了雇主的支持；结果，许多货栈不得不关闭。
还有一次艇户罢工值得注意。这是由于每艘艇每天征收30分附加税引起的。
另外两次重要的罢工也需要记录：米业罢工和丝业罢工。
孙中山政府曾多次对大米批发商和零售商征税，程度之深使得广州的大米价格翻倍。此外，大元帅试图以米商为代价来补充军队给养。士兵被部署在大米卸载地点，他们 seizing（夺取）所需之物。面对此类滥用职权的行为，商人决定不再向广州进口大米。由于本地生产不足，人们担心会出现粮食短缺。罢工运动的领袖与其妻儿一同被暗杀。
丝绸商人受到的税收更重。在这种情况下，资方与劳方完全和谐一致。停工纯粹是为了等待当地商会提交给大元帅解决的纠纷得到处理。
披肩制造商不得不按照当局规定，对其店铺库存进行盘点。在大多数情况下，他们已采取必要预防措施，并与作为客户的欧洲公司安排，将其大部分重要库存转移隐藏。为了保护自己免受警察搜查，其中一些人雇佣了印度看守，仅凭其外貌就足以让调查人员保持距离。
孙中山宣布，发票和其他文件上的官方印花在自由的广东共和国不被承认，当局采取措施强迫银行家和商人（华人）购买一批南方印花，这些印花只是中国其他地区常用印花的仿制品。银行家们决定，如果该措施不撤销，他们将关门停业。这一威胁产生了效果，不久之后，这项

measure which threatened to cut off all credit for a
Government of which it had already so little was withdrawn.
These different measures and the strikes which had
resulted therefrom resulted only in increasing the difficulties
of the population in the province and in Canton particularly.
The Government could not obtain the results that it had
expected and the end of the year found the treasury of the
Government as empty as at the beginning. Employers and
employees resisted to the utmost the demands of the masters at
Canton. Up to the present there had been no efforts made to
effect an alliance between the various professions to unite
in opposition against the importunities of the Government.
The merchant militia representing a force of about 10,000 men
well equipped and properly armed had remained inactive and
was occupied only in protecting the commercial roads against
thieves. It had never been employed against the soldiers and
the military plunderers who had been ravaging certain parts
of the town.
The General Association of Syndicates in Kwangtung
and the General Union of Syndicates of Kwangtung are always
at loggerheads. A third group was organised by Sie Ying Pak:
"The General Co-operative Society," whose object is to support
the claims of the labourers and to take an active part in
politics, whilst the other two organizations limited their
activities to the labour question only.
The new Constitution of October 10 has provoked much
discontent. Parliament having neglected to take into
consideration the proposals formulated with a view to
incorporating them in the text of the Constitution, the
Constitution was not recognized by the Cantonese.

这些不同的措施以及由此引发的罢工，只会增加该省人口，特别是广州人口的困难。
政府未能获得预期的结果，年底时政府国库与年初一样空虚。雇主和雇员极力抵抗广州当局的苛求。到目前为止，尚未做出任何努力使各行业结成联盟，以联合反对政府的纠缠。
代表约一万人的商团，装备精良且武装得当，一直保持 inactive（不活跃/未行动），仅忙于保护商业道路免受盗贼侵扰。它从未被用于对抗那些一直在蹂躏城镇某些地区的士兵和军事掠夺者。
广东总工会和广东工会联合会始终不和。谢英伯（Sie Ying Pak，音译）组织了第三个团体：“总合作社”，其目标是支持劳动者的诉求并积极参与政治，而其他两个组织则将其活动仅限于劳工问题。
10月10日的新宪法引发了诸多不满。由于议会忽视了对旨在纳入宪法文本的建议的考量，该宪法未被广东人承认。

Translation from the "Echo de Chine" of April 3, 1924

THE SOCIAL QUESTION IN KWANGTUNG DURING 1923.
(From the "Politique de Pekin.")
--------------------------
(Continued from yesterday.)

COMMUNISM AND BOLSHEVISM.

The Communist movement in Kwangtung became accentuated during 1923, or at least the Communistic theory served as a pretext and justification for arbitrary acts on the part of the Canton Government against the land-owners. Sun Yat Sen put into operation the theories he had expounded in Japan, whilst he grouped around him revolutionaries and enemies of the Manchu Dynasty. He maintained that property can not and ought not to remain indefinitely in the same hands: in a word the soil belongs to the nation and the State was justified in seizing a part of the most valuable of the land which the owner had held for several years. The owner will have the right to be reimbursed at the price when the purchase was effected and to a third of the value secured. The balance goes to the people, the nation, to the State although it would not be difficult to differentiate one from the other.

Relying upon these principles the Government of Sun Yat Sen during the year proceeded with a number of operations which turned out to be most profitable. The Nation, the State and Sun Yat Sen were confused, the funds realized disappeared into foreign banks in the names of those who had the initiative to put into practice the theory of the "Great Demolisher," as the Chinese now designated Sun Yat Sen.

The movement started with the seizure of the goods of the religious bodies. Temples were sold by auction. Collectors found an exceptional occasion to secure Buddhas, divinities, wooden statues and other ornaments of temples. All was considered as the property of the State was sold at the best price possible in the interests of the liquidators. The Mayor of Canton started the lead and this has enabled him to acquire in Hongkong beautiful estates.

Elated at its first success and turning a deaf ear to the vehement protestations of the people, who saw with pain the disappearance of their sanctuaries, Sun Yat Sen proceeded to deal with private property.

Three systems were applied.

First of all the right of the land-owner to the property adjacent to the temples was challenged. To justify the action of the Government in taking back the property, they had to furnish proof of their ownership. This in China is generally easy enough where title deeds are religiously kept in the family. But in the present circumstances it was practically impossible to act against the principles laid down by the authorities charged with this work. The neighbouring temple was built during the Ming Dynasty, claim the authorities, and it covered a very much larger area than the present one. The holder is then suspected of having appropriated State land. The land is taken away from you; it is but justice. No amount of argument will avail: the prison awaits those who protest. The criminality places the burden upon the holder to prove to the contrary. If by chance he can produce the title deeds as far as the

1923年广东的社会问题。
（摘自《北京政治》（Politique de Pekin）。）
--------------------------
（接昨日。）

共产主义与布尔什维主义。

1923年间，广东的共产主义运动变得突出，或者说，至少共产主义理论被用作广东政府对地主采取任意行为的借口和理由。孙中山实施了他在日本阐述的理论，同时在他周围聚集了革命者和满清王朝的敌人。他坚持认为，财产不能也不应该无限期地保留在同一人手中：简言之，土地属于国家，政府有权没收所有者持有多年的最有价值土地的一部分。所有者有权按购买时的价格获得赔偿，并获得增值部分的三分之一。余额归人民、民族、国家所有，尽管区分这三者并不困难。

依靠这些原则，孙中山政府在这一年进行了一系列操作，结果证明非常有利可图。民族、国家和孙中山被混为一谈，实现的资金以那些主动实施“大破坏者”（中国人现在这样称呼孙中山）理论的人的名义存入了外国银行。

这场运动始于没收宗教团体的财产。寺庙被拍卖。收藏家们发现了一个难得的机会来获取佛像、神像、木雕和其他寺庙装饰品。所有被视为国家财产的物品都以有利于清算人的最高可能价格出售。广州市长带头这样做，这使他得以在香港购置漂亮的地产。

初战告捷令其得意忘形，并对民众看到圣地消失而感到痛苦的强烈抗议充耳不闻，孙中山进而着手处理私有财产。

采用了三种制度。

首先，挑战土地所有者对寺庙相邻财产的权利。为了证明政府收回财产的举动是正当的，所有者必须提供所有权证明。这在中国通常很容易，因为地契通常在家族中被虔诚地保存。但在目前的情况下，实际上不可能违背负责此项工作的当局所制定的原则。当局声称，邻近的寺庙建于明代，其占地面积比现在大得多。因此，持有人被怀疑侵占了国有土地。土地被从你手中夺走；这是公正的。任何辩论都无济于事：监狱等待着那些抗议的人。有罪推定将举证责任倒置给持有人，要求其证明相反情况。如果他碰巧能拿出直到

pages.en:
-8-
epoch named, he wil' bo told that the temple had no right
to sell the land which had been given to it for the needs
of the cult. The result is always the same.
Another method would be to insist upon the production
of the title deed for new registration, all previous registrations being declared null and void, or the title
deeds are detained and the owner is told to produce a sum of
money representing the present day value of the land, or
perhaps a case is brought against him by an individual who
claims a right to the land. Naturally the agent in the pay
of the Municipality always wins the case, the owner is
deported and the land is sold for the benefit of the State.
The last method is still more perfect than the others.
Canton is built on alluvial soil. Now, the deposits of the
river belong to the State, therefore all the lands in Canton
must be State property which may at any time take possession
and do with it what it will. Certain sections have been sold
in this manner. The proprietors have done all they could to
escape as much as possible from these expropriations on the
plea that the lands had been hypothecated or leased out on
long terms. But four bureaux having declared themselves as
competent to proceed with the enregistration, the owners
have to pay very heavily for their complacency and even then
they are not assured against all dangers. The Civil Governor,
the Finance Ministry, the Court of Appeal and the Cadastral
Office accept the registrations, and as there exists no means
of communication between these offices, one is thus faced with
several persons of various authority.
Appended is a summary of a Communist proclamation
such as has often appeared:-

"Following the example of Soviet Russia, the war which
we are undertaking has for its object the procurement of
the daily bread of the citizens. Help us in this war
against the capitalists and the leading militarists.
Farmers, labourers, artisans! Unite and join us.
Here is our programme:-
1) The earth and the fields ought to be the
property of the labourers, without any compensation
to the present proprietors. The Government will
lease the lands out to labourers at $1.50 per mow
per year; lands of second quality will be leased at
$1 per mow per year and those of third quality at
$0.50 per mow per year.
2) The industrial establishments to the
labourers without any charges paid to the proprietors,
on the payment of the local tax of $0.80 cents per
month, and $0.40 and $0.20 according to grades.
3) Shops and factories to the employees upon
the payment to the State of a tax of $0.50 to $1.50
per month according to grades and the location.
4) The nationalisation of banks with the
central administration vested in the Government.
Issue of bank notes at the lowest rate of $1 per
head of the population, equivalent to $400,000,000.
Thus may the capitalists be ousted.
5) Nationalisations of the means of
communications and free transportation for all.
6) Nationalisation of materials and cereals,
the State to undertake the distribution.
7) As the land belongs to the State it cannot
be sold.

This is only one of the most reasonable
examples chosen from amongst those which could be obtained
at meetings or on the street. There are others more absurd still

在上述时期，他会被告知，寺庙无权出售为宗教活动需要而赠予它的土地。结果总是一样。
另一种方法是坚持要求出示地契以进行新登记，宣布所有先前的登记无效，或者扣留地契并告知业主需缴纳一笔相当于土地当前价值的款项，又或者由声称拥有该土地权利的个人对他提起诉讼。自然，受雇于工部局的代理人总是赢得诉讼，业主被驱逐，土地被出售以利于国家。
最后一种方法比其他方法更为完善。广州建在冲积土壤上。现在，河流的沉积物属于国家，因此广州的所有土地必须是国家财产，国家可以随时占有并随意处置。某些地段已以这种方式出售。地主们竭尽全力，以土地已抵押或长期租赁为由，试图尽可能逃避这些征用。但是，由于四个局宣称自己有权进行登记，业主们不得不为其通融付出沉重代价，即便如此，他们仍无法确保免受所有危险。民政长官、财政部、上诉法院和地籍办公室均接受登记，由于这些机构之间不存在沟通渠道，人们因此面对数个拥有不同权威的人士。
附录是一份经常出现的共产党宣言摘要：-

“效仿苏维埃俄罗斯，我们发动的战争旨在为市民获取每日面包。请帮助我们进行这场反对资本家和主要军阀的战争。农民、劳工、工匠们！团结起来加入我们。以下是我们的纲领：-
1) 土地和田地应归劳动者所有，无需向现有业主支付任何补偿。政府将以每亩每年1.50美元的价格将土地租赁给劳动者；二等土地将以每亩每年1美元的价格租赁，三等土地以每亩每年0.50美元的价格租赁。
2) 工业企业归劳动者所有，无需向业主支付任何费用，只需每月缴纳0.80美分的地方税，并根据等级缴纳0.40和0.20。
3) 商店和工厂归雇员所有，需根据等级和地点向国家每月缴纳0.50至1.50美元的税款。
4) 银行国有化，中央管理权归属政府。按人口每人最低1美元的比率发行钞票，相当于4亿美元。从而可将资本家驱逐。
5) 交通手段国有化，所有人免费运输。
6) 物资和谷物国有化，由国家负责分配。
7) 由于土地属于国家，不得出售。

这仅仅是从在集会或街头获得的众多例子中选出的一个较为合理的例子。还有其他更荒谬的

Although Sun Yat Sen is a follower of Bolshevism, he has
on several occasions expressed to passing Soviet agents
in Canton the fear that he may not realise this perfect
state of civilization. The Chinese people are not sufficiently
instructed and educated to be able to understand it. But he
has never failed to make use of every opportunity to
exhibit his sympathy for Russia. On the occasion of the
death of Lenin, Sun Yat Sen ordered that all flags in
Canton be displayed on public buildings.
In the course of the Kuomintang conference which
took place on January 28, Sun Yat Sen expressed his
condolences to the representative of Soviet Russia in
Canton and indicated that the Bolshevik organization will
be used as a model in the organization of the new

虽然孙中山是布尔什维主义的追随者，但他曾多次向途经广州的苏维埃代理人表示，担心他可能无法实现这种完美的文明状态。中国人民没有受到足够的指导和教育，无法理解它。但他从未错过任何机会展示他对俄罗斯的同情。在列宁逝世之际，孙中山下令在广州的所有公共建筑上悬挂旗帜。
在1月28日举行的国民党会议期间，孙中山向驻广州的苏维埃俄罗斯代表表示哀悼，并表示布尔什维克组织将被用作改组新国民党的模范。由吴铁城 (C. C. Wu, 音译) 翻译了大元帅和鲍罗廷的讲话。

Translation from the "Echo de Chin," April 4, 1924.

THE SOCIAL QUESTION IN KUOMINTANG DURING 1923.
(From the "Politique de Pekin.")
------------------
(Continued from yesterday).

REORGANIZATION OF THE KUOMINTANG PARTY.

It is particularly interesting to note the attempt of Sun Yat Sen to reform the Kuomintang Party which has since some time appeared to be disorganized and breaking to pieces in the same manner as happened with the notorious Tong Meng Housui which played an important role during the first revolution.
The Kuomintang Party, or the People's Party according to the literal translation of the Chinese characters, grew out of the Tong Meng Housui, a secret society founded in Japan by Sun Yat Sen in 1901 with Huang Hsin. It was a sort of free-masonry to which belonged as members the larger part of politicians in China and more than half of the Governors of the provinces.
The revolutionaries or Kuomintang mixed with all parties. It was an organization created with the object of fighting against the Manchu Government and against the Ching Dynasty. If it had a political object, it was not, properly speaking, a political party. It was, in short, a coalition against the common enemy, the Manchus. It aimed at the destruction of the existing state of affairs, but it had no definite plan of reconstruction.
It was very powerful during the period of the revolution and in the first months of the Republic, that is to say, during the destructive period. It did not depart from this line of conduct and placed itself in control of the situation when the time for reconstruction arrived. Its very advanced socialistic tendencies, the Tong Meng Housui frightened many of the politicians and the intransigence of some of its followers alienated much sympathy. People feared it, detested it. As its authority diminished, fell to pieces. In Parliament it made itself ridiculous by its violence, a violence caused by its extremist members the majority of whom were Cantonese. To check this threatening disintegration, the leaders of the Kuomintang conceived the idea of reorganizing the association by turning it into a political party. It is this political party, which grew out of the Tong Meng Housui, that came into existence in August, 1913 under the name of the Kuomintang the organization of which was definitely supported by Sun Yat Sen and Huang Hsin whilst on a visit to Peking. In truth, the true creator of the party was Sung Chiao Jen, the Minister of Agriculture in the first Republican Cabinet, who was assassinated shortly before the opening of the Republican Parliament. At this time the programme of the party might be summarised as follows:-
The maintenance of unity between the north and the south.
The maintenance of territorial integrity.
The formation of a strong central government.
The most complete autonomy for the provinces so that in the event of the central government being incompetent, a federation of provinces could replace it.
Social reforms and compulsory public education.
To improve the agricultural and mineral resources of the country.
Equality of race and of peoples.
Religious freedom.

译自1924年4月4日《中国回声报》(Echo de Chin)。

1923年国民党内的社会问题。
（摘自《北京政治》(Politique de Pekin)。）
------------------
（接昨日）。

国民党的改组。

特别值得注意的是孙中山改革国民党的尝试，该党似乎在一段时间内显得组织涣散并分崩离析，就像在第一次革命中扮演重要角色的著名同盟会 (Tong Meng Housui) 所发生的那样。
国民党，或按汉字直译为“人民党”，起源于同盟会，这是一个由孙中山和黄兴于1901年在日本成立的秘密社团。它类似于一种共济会，其成员包括中国大部分政客和超过半数的各省督军。
革命者或国民党人与各党派混杂在一起。它是一个旨在反对满清政府和清朝的组织。如果它有政治目标，严格来说，它不是一个政党。简而言之，它是针对共同敌人满人的联盟。它旨在破坏现有局势，但没有明确的重建计划。
它在革命期间和共和国最初几个月，即破坏时期，非常强大。当重建时期到来时，它并未偏离这一行为路线，并控制了局势。其非常先进的社会主义倾向，同盟会吓坏了许多政客，其部分追随者的不妥协态度疏远了许多同情者。人们害怕它，憎恨它。随着其权威减弱，分崩离析。在议会中，它因其暴力行为而变得可笑，这种暴力是由其极端主义成员造成的，其中大多数是广东人。为了遏制这种威胁性的分裂，国民党领导人构思了通过将其转变为政党来重组该协会的想法。这个从同盟会发展而来的政党，于1913年8月在孙中山和黄兴访问北京期间正式成立，其组织得到了他们的坚定支持。事实上，该党的真正创建者是宋教仁，他是第一届共和内阁的农业总长，在共和议会开幕前不久被暗杀。当时，该党的纲领可概括如下：-
维持南北统一。
维护领土完整。
建立强有力的中央政府。
给予各省最完全的自治权，以便在中央政府无能时，可由各省联邦取而代之。
社会改革和强制公共教育。
改善国家的农业和矿产资源。
种族和人民平等。
宗教自由。

pages.en:
-2-

In fact it was a party of advanced socialists, although its
extreme left was composed of Communists and Cantonese of
political equality.
The Kuomintang absorbed the Republican Coalition Party
(Tong Meng Housi), the National Democrat Party (Kuo Ming Kong
Tang) and the Society of Union and Progress (Kong Ho Yie Tain
Houei). It constituted the bulk of social-democrats under the
active and intelligent direction of its chief, Sun Chao Jen.
It acted in opposition to the Conservative Party and to the
Republican Reform Party which it proposed to fight for influence
in Parliament. It was the Kuomintang, or rather the advanced
group of the party which let loose the second revolution the
failure of which compelled Sun Yat Sen, Huang Hsin and their
followers to seek refuge in Japan.
The fact that the name had been modified did not change
the mentality of the leaders of the Kuomintang who preserved
the principles of the Tong Meng Houei. On November 4, 1913
Yuan Shih Kai ordered the dissolution of the party as being
dangerous to public order and security. It did not appear
again until the convocation of the 1912 Parliament by Li Yuan
Hung in 1916. The party again gave evidence of its incompetency,
its violence, its ignorance of the needs of the nation.

Noisy and squabbling, it paralysed all initiative, obstructed
commerce and provoked anew the measures adopted by the northern
militarists for the dissolution of a party which has only
spread its useless agitation and disordered ambition.
It was the Kuomintang who constituted the "Emigrating
Parliament" which moved away from Peking to Nanking, Shanghai,
Canton and Yunnan and which would probably have gone to
Chungking if Tang Chi Yao had not been forced to evacuate
Szechuen. The only trustees, as they claimed, of Constitutional
Government, they carried out in China a sort of touring
exhibition. They went wherever it was expected that they
would be paid for representing the nation, although in a number
of cases their term of service had already expired. Discredited
but still proud of a title to which they had no right whatever,
these representatives of the Chinese people carried in their
bags inflammatory speeches, utopian ideas, common place topics,
bringing disorder wherever they went, criticising everything
but themselves incapable of doing anything. From this arose
the division of the Kuomintang Party into three groups: the
Right, the Centre and the Left.
The Right represented the conservative elements, similar
to the ancient Progressive Reform Party of Kiang Yu Wei and
Liang Chi Chao and comparable to the Liberal Republican Party
of Tsai Ao and Tang Chi Yao. In Kwangtung, Liang Chi Chao is
regarded as a monarchist.
The Centre comprises moderate socialists. It seeks an
alliance with the new Communications Party formed by Yeh Kung
Cho, former Minister of Communications in Peking, and an
ex-Minister of Finances in Sun Yat Sen's Government. It tries
to secure the support of Chang Tso Lin and flirts with Japan.
To this section of the Party belongs Chen Chuin Ming, C. C. Wu,
who is in charge of the foreign affairs of Sun's Government,
and Chao Li, the Director of Finances and others. But it is a
delicate matter to state definitely that such and such a person
belongs to such and such a Party. Opinions in China, and in
Kwangtung above all, are dictated by personal and immediate
considerations. The dollar plays a preponderant role, and it
is liable to provoke most unexpected alliances or desertions.
Convictions do not matter in the face of golden ambition.
The Left has definite Communist and Bolshevik tendencies,
Sun Yat Sen, Sun Fo and E. Cheng being the leaders who are
associated Sie Ying Pack, the great director of syndicates,
and notorious Communist. These extremists have worked to secure
the support of the mass of the people. Their advanced socialism

事实上，它是一个先进社会主义者的政党，尽管其极左翼由共产主义者和主张政治平等的广东人组成。
国民党吸收了共和党联盟 (Tong Meng Housi, 音译)、国家民主党 (Kuo Ming Kong Tang, 音译) 和统一进步会 (Kong Ho Yie Tain Houei, 音译)。在其领袖宋教仁 (Sun Chao Jen, 原文如此，应为宋教仁 Song Jiaoren) 积极而明智的指导下，它构成了社会民主派的主体。
它与保守党和共和改革党对立，并提议在议会中争夺影响力。正是国民党，或者更确切地说是党内的激进派，发动了第二次革命，其失败迫使孙中山、黄兴及其追随者寻求避难于日本。
名称的改变并没有改变国民党领导人的心态，他们保留了同盟会的原则。1913年11月4日，袁世凯命令解散该党，理由是危害公共秩序和安全。直到1916年黎元洪召集1912年议会时，该党才再次出现。该党再次表现出其无能、暴力以及对国家需求的无知。

喧闹且争吵不休，它瘫痪了所有主动性，阻碍了商业，并再次引发了北方军阀为解散一个仅散布无用煽动和混乱野心的政党而采取的措施。
正是国民党组成了“流亡议会”，该议会从北京迁往南京、上海、广州和云南，如果不是唐继尧被迫撤离四川，它可能会去重庆。作为他们自称的宪政政府的唯一受托人，他们在中国进行了一种巡回展览。他们前往任何预计会因代表国家而获得报酬的地方，尽管在许多情况下，他们的任期已经届满。这些中国人民的代表虽信誉扫地，但仍为他们毫无权利享有的头衔感到自豪，他们的行囊里装着煽动性演讲、乌托邦思想和陈词滥调，所到之处带来混乱，批评一切，但自身却无力做任何事情。由此导致国民党分裂为三个派系：右派、中间派和左派。
右派代表保守元素，类似于康有为和梁启超的古老进步改革党，并可比作蔡锷和唐继尧的自由共和党。在广东，梁启超被视为君主主义者。
中间派包括温和社会主义者。它寻求与由前北京交通总长、孙中山政府的前财政部长叶恭绰 (Yeh Kung Cho, 音译) 组建的新交通系结盟。它试图争取张作霖的支持，并与日本眉来眼去。陈炯明 (Chen Chuin Ming, 音译)、负责孙政府外交事务的吴铁城 (C. C. Wu, 音译) 以及财政总监赵理 (Chao Li, 音译) 等人属于该派系。但是，明确断定某人属于某党是一件微妙的事情。在中国，尤其是在广东，意见受个人和即时考虑的支配。美元起着主导作用，并可能引发最意想不到的联盟或背叛。在金色的野心面前，信念无关紧要。
左派具有明确的共产主义和布尔什维克倾向，孙中山、孙科和陈友仁 (E. Cheng, 音译) 是与工会大主管、著名共产主义者谢英伯 (Sie Ying Pack, 音译) 有关的领导人。这些极端分子致力于争取广大群众的支持。他们的先进社会主义

has turned the labour syndicates into lying dogs ready to
do everything for the "Great Master." The successes of
the strikes last year have naturally secured ardent
followers ready to sacrifice themselves, despite the well
known cowardice of the Cantonese, had not Sun Yat Sen and
his lieutenants curbed the syndicates. The forced
recruiting of "volunteers" for service at the front, the
requisition of coolies to carry arms and ammunition, the
contributions which the syndicates were compelled to make
to enable Sun Yat Sen live in Canton—all these had somewhat
cooled the ardour of the syndicates. Communism in theory is
very fascinating so long as the capitalist-bourgeois is
deprived of their belongings, but when, as in China, every
body possesses a little plot of land in the country and sees
himself despoiled of it under one pretext or another, it
becomes less seductive; even a tottering hovel in the city
the police will put in a d rank in the name of the
Government for $100, quite a fortune to him, and if after 15
days he has not yet satisfied the demand, he will find
himself deported and his property sold by auction. The
labourers, therefore, has little love for a theory which
allows what is known as "requisitioning" but which he calls
"theft," now that he himself is being made the victim. He
will not dare to raise his voice too high for they will
shoot without examination in the idiom of the south.
The advanced elements of the Kuomintang Party realise
full well that they are not enjoying the sympathy of the
people, that the party is threatened with ruin, that the
germ of dissolution which had permeated the party at the time
of its formation was spreading and that there is in an
inert section of the party (the right and the centre)
a recoil which was continuing to evolve with disconcerting
rapidity. Being in the minority it is normal that they
impose their will. They therefore decided to proceed with
the reorganization and the reinforcement of the Party. Sun
Yat Sen undertook this reorganization with a view to the
new revolution which he was planning and of which he has
already spoken on several occasions. He has innovated
no principles. He has taken and adapted them to the new
conditions the regulations of the Tong Meng Hueil. The
Kuomintang Party thus modified or renovated becomes
practically a secret society. Perhaps his friends, the
Bolsheviks, have provided with a detailed plan of soviet
organization. M. Borodine, the guest of the Southern
Government, can, in this respect, furnish the Generalissimo
with the formation on the branches operating at Tanshan No. 18.
The Tong Meng Hueil, which was a sort of free-masonry, with
correspondence lodges in all the provinces of China and a
central lodge at Peking, finds its second self in the reorganized
Kuomintang Party with, however, this difference: the Grand
Masters are replaced by elected committees. Thus there is a
complete hierarchy of committees.
At the bottom and representing the component element of
the Party is the local club (lodge or soviet) composed of
at least four members. It elects three members as a Committee
which selects a secretary to deal with routine business and
to furnish reports every fortnight. To this club falls the
duties of securing followers, helping the divisional
Committees, choosing or electing the members of the general
assembly of the division, of the general provincial
conference and the General National Conference. It receives
subscriptions and collections and provides the sale of stamps,
photographs and commemorative pictures. It must act in
strict conformity with instructions received from the
superior bodies. The local club must be approved by the
District Committee.
The Divisional Committee is sprung from the General
Assembly of the Division. It has control over the local

已将劳工辛迪加变成了唯“大师”马首是瞻、甘愿为其效犬马之劳的走狗。去年罢工的胜利自然赢得了热衷于自我牺牲的追随者，尽管众所周知广东人素来怯懦，若非孙中山及其部下心腹对辛迪加加以遏制，局势恐更甚。强制征募“志愿者”赴前线服役，强征苦力运送军火弹药，以及迫使辛迪加分摊捐款以维持孙中山在广州的生活——所有这一切都在一定程度上冷却了辛迪加的热情。从理论上讲，只要剥夺资本家资产阶级的财产，共产主义就极具吸引力；但是，当像在中国这样，每个人在乡下都拥有一小块土地，却看到自己因各种借口而被剥夺时，它就不再那么诱人了；即使是城里一间摇摇欲坠的棚屋，警方也会以政府的名义将其估价为100美元——对他来说这是一笔巨款——如果他在15天后仍未满足这一要求，他将被驱逐出境，其财产将被拍卖。因此，劳工们对自己成为受害者的所谓“征用”（他们称之为“盗窃”）的理论并无好感。他们不敢大声疾呼，因为按照南方的习惯，当局会不经审讯直接开枪。

国民党的激进分子充分意识到，他们并未获得民众的同情，党面临崩溃的威胁，建党之初便渗透进党内的瓦解因子正在蔓延，且党内惰性部分（右派和中间派）出现的反弹正以令人不安的速度持续演变。作为少数派，他们强行推行自己的意志是正常的。因此，他们决定着手改组和加强党组织。孙中山为了他策划的新革命进行了这次改组，对此他已多次提及。他并未创新任何原则，而是根据同盟会的规章，适应新形势加以采纳和调整。经过如此修改或革新的国民党，实际上变成了一个秘密会社。也许他的朋友布尔什维克提供了一份详细的苏维埃组织计划。南方政府的客人鲍罗廷先生（M. Borodine）在这方面可以向总司令提供关于在唐山路18号运作的分支机构的情报。同盟会是一种类似共济会的组织，在中国各省设有通信分部，在北京设有中央分部，它在改组后的国民党中找到了其翻版，但有一个区别：大导师被选举产生的委员会所取代。因此，存在一个完整的委员会层级体系。

处于底层并代表党的构成要素的是地方俱乐部（分部或苏维埃），由至少四名成员组成。它选举三名成员组成委员会，该委员会选出一名秘书处理日常事务并每两周提交报告。该俱乐部的职责包括招募追随者、协助分区委员会、选择或选举分区大会、全省代表大会和全国代表大会的成员。它接收会费和捐款，并负责销售邮票、照片和纪念图片。它必须严格按照上级机构收到的指示行事。地方俱乐部必须经区委员会批准。

分区委员会产生于分区大会。它管辖其辖区内的地方

clubs formed within its jurisdiction. It must send to the
District Committee every fortnight a report of its labours
and of all questions of a nature that may interest the party.
The District Committee is a product of the General Assembly
of the District. It must meet every week and send in a
monthly report to the Provincial Committee. It has authority
over the district clubs and the local clubs to which it
transmits the orders of the Party. It deals with the finances
of the various branches within its jurisdiction and selects
the personnel to take charge of the official newspaper of the
Party in the district.
The Provincial committee which is elected by the General
Provincial Conference, meets every fifteen days. It supervises
and directs all the sections previously described. It sends in
to the Central Committee a report of its work once a month.
The Central Committee is the brain of the Party. It is
elected by the General National Conference and holds its
meetings under the presidency of the chief of the Party. It
is from there that all orders are transmitted to the Provincial
Committees, thence to the Divisional Committees, which in turn
pass them on to the local clubs.
The programme of the new Party is to establish an era of
absolute freedom and to achieve this it is ordained by one of
the regulations (Art. 53) that strict discipline and implicit
obedience to orders received are indispensable. The members
must occupy themselves with the formation of groups in the heart
of labour syndicates, unions, associations, clubs, schools,
assemblies, provincial assemblies, Parliament and also in
secret societies in such a way as to extend the influence of the
Party and to make it permeate everything.
Women may be admitted as members of the Party. Their
admission must be made on the recommendation of two members of
the Party and the candidature must be submitted for approval
to the general conference of the Kuomintang Party. The new
member promises to observe the regulations of the Party, and to
obey strictly its orders and decisions and to pay his fees
which are fixed at $0.50 per month. Disciplinary measures will
be taken against those who violate the regulations or against
those who refuse to accept the orders given.
These general regulations give no indication whatever of
the organization of the superior committee of administrators
elected by the General National Conference.
The new Kuomintang Party appeals to the soldiers to join
and help the Party in its social battle. They are today the
first victims of capitalism, having been set one against the other
They are asked also to assist the nation in regaining its
complete independence. China today is the vassal of the European
capitalists who regard it as a country of semi-sovereignty and
compels her to buy their products--products which China does
not need, her own resources being more than sufficient if only
they can be improved and exploited by her own people without the
assistance of foreign capitalists.
The commercial and industrial hold of the Powers, herein
lies the true danger to China and which is preventing the
re-establishment of peace.
Whatever his shortcomings may be, Sun Yat Sen knows the
vulnerable points of the Chinese people, and he does not hesitate
for the purpose of strengthening and reconstructing his crumbling
Party, to agitate anew the spectre of foreign menace.
This is the only thing that he can make use of at present after
putting to the sack the province of Kwangtung and after having
exhibited, on a scale unprecedented hitherto, a sample of his
leadership as chief pirate.

俱乐部。它必须每两周向区委员会提交一份关于其工作及所有可能引起党感兴趣的问题的报告。区委员会是区大会的产物。它必须每周开会，并向省委员会提交月度报告。它对区俱乐部和地方俱乐部拥有权威，并向它们传达党的命令。它处理其辖区内各分支机构的财务，并挑选人员负责该区党的官方报纸。

省委员会由省代表大会选举产生，每十五天开会一次。它监督和指导前述所有部门。它每月向中央委员会提交一次工作报告。中央委员会是党的大脑。它由全国代表大会选举产生，并在党魁的主持下召开会议。所有命令均由此传达到省委员会，再传达到分区委员会，进而传达到地方俱乐部。

新党的纲领是建立一个绝对自由的时代，为了实现这一目标，其中一项规章（第53条）规定，严格的纪律和对所收命令的绝对服从是必不可少的。党员必须致力于在劳工辛迪加、工会、协会、俱乐部、学校、集会、省议会、国会以及秘密会社内部建立小组，以便扩大党的影响力，使其渗透到各个方面。

妇女可以被接纳为党员。她们的入党必须由两名党员推荐，并将候选人资格提交国民党大会批准。新成员承诺遵守党的规章，严格服从其命令和决定，并缴纳每月固定为0.50美元的会费。对违反规章或拒绝接受命令的人将采取纪律措施。

这些一般规章完全没有提及由全国代表大会选举产生的高级行政委员会的组织情况。

新国民党呼吁士兵加入并帮助党进行社会斗争。他们今天是资本主义的首要受害者，彼此被置于对立地位。他们还被要求协助国家恢复完全独立。中国如今是欧洲资本家的附庸，后者视中国为半主权国家，并强迫中国购买其产品——这些产品是中国并不需要的，如果仅由中国人民在没有外国资本家协助的情况下改善和开发，其自身资源绰绰有余。

列强在商业和工业上的控制，构成了对中国真正的危险，并阻碍了和平的重建。

无论孙中山有何缺点，他都深知中国人的弱点，并且为了加强和重建其摇摇欲坠的政党，毫不犹豫地再次煽动外来威胁的幽灵。

在洗劫广东省之后，并以迄今未有的规模展示了他作为头号海盗首领的领导才能之后，这是目前他唯一可以利用的手段。

The advanced elements of the Kuomintang Party, but
relatively moderate when compared with those who compose
the court of the "Lord of Can", retired from a
Government which they see openly despoiling the people
they are supposed to protect and direct.
It is for this reason that Sun Yat Sen, seeing the
party lost, was only too happy to bring in the factor of
the hostility of the Powers to abandon a country which he
had ruined and which he had administered by means of terror.
He thus retired with a certain amount of "face" from a
situation which appeared to be at that time without solution.

THE SOCIAL QUESTION IN KWANGTUNG DURING 1923.
(From the "Politique de Pekin.")
------------------
(continued from yesterday)

THE NEW REGULATIONS OF THE KUOMINTANG PARTY.

Chapter I.--- Members.

Art. 1. Whoever observes those regulations, submits himself to the Committee, obeys its orders and decisions, and pays a fee becomes a member of the Party.
Art. 2. To be admitted, it is sufficient that a candidate be introduced by two members of the Party who will guarantee the candidate.
Art. 3. The candidate is admitted on the day that the General Conference of the Party approves of his candidature.
Art. 4. All members who enter a province must make themselves known to the local branch and register themselves.

Chapter II. Organization of the Party.

Art. 5. The Grand Council has control over local organizations.
Art. 6. The assembly has the right to deal with all local affairs that are within its province.
Art. 7. The General National Conference of Delegates, the Local General Conference of Delegates and the General Conference of members may give orders to the assemblies.
Art. 8. These three Conferences will elect the Committee of Directors.
Art. 9. The organization of assemblies will be as follows:-
a) For the whole country, the General National Conference of Delegates forms the Central Committee of management.
b) For the province, the General Provincial Conference of Delegates forms the Provincial Committee.
c) For the district, the General District Conference of Delegates forms the District Committee.
d) For the section, the General Conference Conference of Delegates of the Section forms the Committee of the Section.
e) Below the section the General Conference of Members appoints the local committee.
Art. 10. Authority is distributed as follows:-
a) The Central Committee represents the General National Conference of Delegates.
b) The Provincial Committee represents the General Provincial Conference.
c) The District Committee represents the General District Conference.
d) The Sectional Committee represents the General Conference of the Section.
e) The Local Committee represents the General Conference of Local Delegates.
They possess respectively authority to organize to draw up regulations, and to enforce them rigorously after they have been referred to the superior authority.
Art. 11. The Central Committee, the Provincial Committee etc. are authorised to establish the various departments to deal with routine or extraordinary matters, but the departments thus created must follow strictly the instructions of the Central Committee.

1923年广东的社会问题。
（摘自《北京政治》。）
------------------
（接昨日）

国民党新规章。

第一章.--- 党员。

第1条. 凡遵守本规章、服从委员会、听从其命令和决定并缴纳会费者，即成为本党党员。
第2条. 候选人只要有两名党员介绍并为其担保，即可被接纳。
第3条. 候选人在党的大会批准其候选人资格之日被接纳。
第4条. 所有进入某省的党员必须向当地分支机构报到并注册。

第二章. 党的组织。

第5条. 总理事会管辖地方组织。
第6条. 大会有权处理其职权范围内的所有地方事务。
第7条. 全国代表代表大会、地方代表代表大会和党员大会可向各大会议下达命令。
第8条. 这三大会议将选举指导委员会。
第9条. 各大会议的组织如下：-
a) 对于全国，全国代表代表大会组成中央管理委员会。
b) 对于省，省代表代表大会组成省委员会。
c) 对于区，区代表代表大会组成区委员会。
d) 对于分部，分部代表代表大会组成分部委员会。
e) 在分部之下，由党员大会任命地方委员会。
第10条. 权力分配如下：-
a) 中央委员会代表全国代表代表大会。
b) 省委员会代表省代表大会。
c) 区委员会代表区代表大会。
d) 分部委员会代表分部大会。
e) 地方委员会代表地方代表大会。
它们分别拥有组织权、制定规章权，并在报请上级批准后严格执行这些规章。
第11条. 中央委员会、省委员会等有权设立各部门以处理日常或特殊事务，但由此设立的部门必须严格遵守中央委员会的指示。

Art. 12. The sub-sections, the local sections are directed
by the Provincial Committee which in its turn is under the
direction of the Central Committee.
Art. 13. Sectional Committees and local Committees must
first of all be recognized by the superior authority before
they can function.
Art. 14. All members must carry the certificate issued by
the Provincial Committee. These certificates are drawn up by
the Central Committee.

Chapter III. Administration.

Art. 15. Superior authority is vested in the General National
Conference of Delegates which meets every year. However, a
General National Conference of Delegates may be held should the
Central Committee deems it necessary or at the demand of
one-third of the delegates present at the last general conference.
Art. 16. The date and the programme of the General National
Conference of Delegates must be made known to those interested
two months before the opening, and three months in advance in
the case of extraordinary conferences.
Art. 17. The General National Conference of Delegates is in
quorum if half the number of members attending the last
Conference is present.
Art. 18. The organization of a General Conference and the
number of delegates will be provisionally fixed by the Central
Committee.
Art. 19. The powers and duties of the national conference
are as follows:-
a) To receive and examine the reports of the Central
Committee and of the various departments
under it.
b) To amend the regulations and plans.
c) To examine actual political and administrative
problems.
d) To elect chairmen of Committees, the members of the
committees and the supervisors.
Art. 20. The members of the Central Committee and of the
Committee of Control are elected by the General National
Conference.
Art. 21. They are empowered to replace members of the
Committee by candidates on the waiting list.
Art. 22. The powers and the privileges of the Central
Committee are:-
a) To represent the Party in its foreign relations.
b) To organise local assemblies and to direct them.
c) To appoint the staff of the official newspaper of
the Party.
d) To organise the various assemblies dependent upon
the Central Committee.
e) Income and expenditure.
Art. 23. The Central Committee supervises the offices of
the directors, the assemblies, societies, syndicates, Chambers
of Commerce, municipal assemblies, provincial assemblies, the
Senate, the Chamber of Deputies and the special unions of the
Kuomintang Party.
Art. 24. The Central Committee meets at least every fifteen
days and expectant candidates who have the right to speak may
be admitted.
Art. 25. The Chairmanship of the Central Committee is held
by the leader of the Party.
Art. 26. The Central Committee elects nine secretaries who
have to organize a secretariat to undertake routine duties.
Art. 27 It is the duty of the Central Committee to summon
the Provincial Committees, to appoint delegates and representatives
of assemblies to the General National Conference.

第十二条。各分部及地方分部受省委员会指导，而省委员会又受中央委员会指导。
第十三条。分部委员会和地方委员会必须首先获得上级机关的认可，方可开展工作。
第十四条。所有成员必须持有由省委员会颁发的证书。这些证书由中央委员会制定。

第三章。行政。

第十五条。最高权力属于每年召开一次的全国代表大会。然而，如果中央委员会认为有必要，或应上一次大会出席代表的三分之一要求，也可召开全国代表大会。
第十六条。全国代表大会的日期和议程必须在会议召开前两个月通知有关各方；如遇特别会议，则须提前三个月通知。
第十七条。如有上次大会出席代表人数的一半到场，全国代表大会即达到法定人数。
第十八条。全国大会的组织形式及代表人数将由中央委员会暂时确定。
第十九条。全国代表大会的职权如下：
a) 接收并审查中央委员会及其下属各部门的报告。
b) 修订规章和计划。
c) 审查实际政治和行政问题。
d) 选举委员会主席、委员会委员及监察员。
第二十条。中央委员会和监察委员会的成员由全国代表大会选举产生。
第二十一条。他们有权用候补名单上的候选人替换委员会成员。
第二十二条。中央委员会的权力和特权如下：
a) 在对外关系中代表本党。
b) 组织地方集会并对其进行指导。
c) 任命本党官方报纸的工作人员。
d) 组织隶属于中央委员会的各种集会。
e) 收支管理。
第二十三条。中央委员会监督国民党各局长办公室、集会、社团、工会、商会、市议会、省议会、参议院、众议院以及特别工会。
第二十四条。中央委员会至少每十五天开会一次，并可准许有发言权的候补候选人列席。
第二十五条。中央委员会主席由党的领袖担任。
第二十六条。中央委员会选举九名秘书，组成秘书处以处理日常事务。
第二十七条。中央委员会有责任召集省委员会，并指派参加全国代表大会的各集会代表和代表。

Art. 28. The Central Committee makes monthly reports on important events to the Provincial Committees etc.

Chapter IV. --- Committee of Control.

Art. 29. The General Conference elects three members to organize a Committee of Control whose powers will be as follows:-
a) To examine the statements of income and expenditure presented by the Central Committee.
b) To examine the accounts of the various organizations dependant upon the Party, to inspect their affairs and to control their work.

Chapter V.---Provincial Conference.

Art. 30. The General Provincial Conference meets every six months. It can meet on the orders of the Central Committee or at the demand of the Sectional Committees.
Art. 31. In case of necessity or at the demand of half of the members provincial of the Party, the Provincial Committee may convene a general provincial conference.
Art. 32. The election and the number of delegates of the Provincial Conference are to be determined by the Provincial Committee in agreement with the Districts Committees.
Art. 33. The General Provincial Conference receives and examines the reports of the Provincial Committee, of the various assemblies in the province and proceeds with the election of the committees.
Art. 34. The Conference has the following powers:-
a) The organization of a secretariat of three persons.
b) The creation of assemblies in the province, and the supervision and direction of those assemblies.
c) The nomination of the staff of the official newspaper of the Party in the province.
d) Income and expenditure.
Art. 35. The Provincial Committee must make a monthly report on its work to the Central Committee.
Art. 36. The Provincial Committee meets every 15 days, to which candidates having authority to speak are admitted.
Art. 37. It is empowered to replace absent members of the Provincial Committee by expectant candidates.
Art. 38. The Provincial Committee of Control examines the statements of income and expenditure and controls the acts of the members of the Party.

Chapter VI.---District Conference.

Art. 39. The General District Conference meets every three months on the orders of the Provincial Committee or at the demand of the delegates of the districts; it can hold extraordinary meetings.
Art. 40. In case of necessity or at the demand of half of the members of the Party in the district, an extraordinary general conference can be held.
Art. 41. The election and the number of members of the General District Conference are determined by the District Committee after investigation and approval of the Provincial Committee.
Art. 42. The General District Conference receives and examines the reports of the District Committee and of the various assemblies of the Party in the Province. It appoints the Committee, the candidates and the controller.

第二十八条。中央委员会就重要事件向省委员会等机构提交月度报告。

第四章。--- 监察委员会。

第二十九条。全国大会选举三名成员组成监察委员会，其职权如下：
a) 审查中央委员会提交的收支报表。
b) 审查隶属于本党的各组织的账目，检查其事务并监督其工作。

第五章。--- 省大会。

第三十条。全省大会每六个月召开一次。它可根据中央委员会的命令或应分部委员会的要求召开。
第三十一条。如有必要，或应本省半数党员的要求，省委员会可召开全省大会。
第三十二条。省大会代表的选举及人数，由省委员会与各区委员会协商确定。
第三十三条。全省大会接收并审查省委员会及省内各集会的报告，并进行委员会的选举。
第三十四条。大会拥有以下权力：
a) 组织一个由三人组成的秘书处。
b) 在省内建立集会，并对这些集会进行监督和指导。
c) 提名本省本党官方报纸的工作人员。
d) 收支管理。
第三十五条。省委员会必须每月向中央委员会报告其工作。
第三十六条。省委员会每15天开会一次，准许有发言权的候选人列席。
第三十七条。它有权用候补候选人替换缺席的省委员会成员。
第三十八条。省监察委员会审查收支报表，并监督党员的行为。

第六章。--- 区大会。

第三十九条。全区大会每三个月根据省委员会的命令或应各区代表的要求召开一次；它可以举行特别会议。
第四十条。如有必要，或应区内半数党员的要求，可召开特别全区大会。
第四十一条。全区大会成员的选举及人数，由区委员会在经省委员会调查批准后确定。
第四十二条。全区大会接收并审查区委员会及省内本党各集会的报告。它任命委员会、候选人和监察员。

Art. 43. The District Committee elects a secretary to perform routine duties, establishes local assemblies, directs them, appoints the staff of the official newspaper, organises assemblies, determines their expenses and their finances after examination and approval by the Provincial Committee.
Art. 44. The District Committee sends a report every eight days to the Provincial Committee.
Art. 45. The District Committee meets every week. The candidates who have the right to speak are admitted.
Art. 46. It has power to replace absent members of the Committee by expectant candidates.

Chapter VII.---Sectional Conferences.
Art. 47. The highest authority in a section is the General Sectional Conference, under it comes the Local Village Committee comprising village members. However, if the village is located too far from town but can assemble a large number of members, it can constitute a conference which will be the highest authority.
Art. 48. Meetings are to be held every month to examine and discuss the following matters:
a) Candidature of those desiring to join the Party.
b) Reports of the District Committee.
c) Solution of pending questions, expression of political ideas, and finances.
d) To secure members, to retain fees, to discuss the decisions of the District Committee and of the Sectional Committee.
e) To elect the committee.
Art. 49. The Sectional Committee directs the local district assemblies or inferior organizations dependent on it, indicates the measures to effect this, calls conventions of citizens, organises local assemblies, and distributes funds in the manner ordered by the District Committee. The Sectional Committee sends in a report every 15 days to the District Committee.

Chapter VIII.---Local or Communal Conference.
Art. 50. The local or communal conference is the elementary organism of the Party. It is organised by the Sectional Committee, but it must be first of all sanctioned by the District Committee. The number of its members must not be less than five.
Art. 51. The Communal Conference serves as a link between the members and the high superior bodies. When there is only one Communal Conference and nothing above it, it is considered as the superior organ. It must (a) secure members; (b) assist the Sectional Committee; (c) Spread the tracts and circulars of the Party; (d) bring in the subscriptions, receive the funds provided by the sale of stamps, photographs and commemorative pictures; (e) Select or elect the delegates to the General Sectional Conference, to the General District Conference, to the General Provincial Conference and to the General National Conference; (f) to comply with the orders of the superior bodies.
Art. 52. The Communal Conference of the section must elect three members to form a committee to attend to daily routine work, this committee elects a secretary to draft a report every fifteen days to be sent to the District Committee.

Chapter IX.---The Law.
Art. 53. The members must strictly observe the law of the Party, and when they occupy an official position in troublous times, they must obey strictly and strive to solve the problems brought to them and to follow faithfully the solution once the line of conduct has been thought out.

第四十四条。区委员会每八天向省委员会提交一份报告。
第四十五条。区委员会每周开会一次。准许有发言权的候选人列席。
第四十六条。它有权用候补候选人替换缺席的委员会成员。

第七章。--- 分部大会。
第四十七条。分部的最高权力机构是分部大会，其下是包括村民成员的地方村委员会。然而，如果村庄距离城镇太远但能聚集大量成员，它可以组成一个作为最高权力机构的会议。
第四十八条。每月举行会议，审查和讨论以下事项：
a) 希望入党者的候选资格。
b) 区委员会的报告。
c) 悬而未决问题的解决、政治思想的表达以及财务问题。
d) 吸纳成员，保留会费，讨论区委员会和分部委员会的决定。
e) 选举委员会。
第四十九条。分部委员会指导隶属于它的地方区集会或下级组织，指示实施措施，召集市民公约，组织地方集会，并按照区委员会命令的方式分配资金。分部委员会每15天向区委员会提交一份报告。

第八章。--- 地方或社区大会。
第五十条。地方或社区大会是本党的基本组织单位。它由分部委员会组织，但必须首先获得区委员会的批准。其成员人数不得少于五人。
第五十一条。社区大会充当成员与高级上级机构之间的纽带。当只有一个社区大会且其上无其他机构时，它被视为上级机构。它必须 (a) 吸纳成员；(b) 协助分部委员会；(c) 散发本党的小册子和通告；(d) 收取认捐款项，接收通过出售邮票、照片和纪念图片提供的资金；(e) 挑选或选举参加分部大会、全区大会、全省大会和全国大会的代表；(f) 遵守上级机构的命令。
第五十二条。该分部的社区大会必须选举三名成员组成一个委员会，负责处理日常例行工作，该委员会选举一名秘书，每十五天起草一份报告送交区委员会。

第九章。--- 纪律。
第五十三条。成员必须严格遵守党的纪律，当他们在动荡时期担任公职时，必须严格服从，努力解决摆在他们面前的问题，并在行动方针确定后忠实地执行既定方案。

Art. 54. Every member who violates the laws of the Party,
who does not carry out its orders or does not appreciate its
virtues will be punished as follows:-
His act will be brought to the notice of all through the
newspapers of the Party. Whilst awaiting a temporary suspension
or definite expulsion, he will be prohibited from holding any
official position.
If several members of the same assembly are guilty of the
same fault, they will be punished as follows:-
All the members of the assembly will register themselves
anew and their exclusion or pardon will be decided.
The assembly may be dissolved and the causes for this action
will be published in all the newspapers of the Party.
Art. 55. Every member or all members of the an assembly
if he or if they are invalidated or considered as undesirables,
after investigation by the Committee of Control and the Communal
Committee may appeal to the Superior Committee as well as to the
General National Conference, but before a decision is given,
they will be considered as invalidated. The General National
Conference will decide whether there should be or should not
be a new member admitted into the Party, subject to the
approval of the Central Committee. Whilst awaiting this decision
of the Central Committee, the decision of the Conference will
not take effect.

Chapter X.---Finances.
Art. 56. The revenue of the Party consists of subscriptions
of the members and the funds collected by the superior bodies
as well as other receipts.
Art. 57. Members must pay 20 cents per month, but in case
of illness or through impecuniosity, members may be authorised
not to pay after advising the local assembly which should refer
the matter to the superior authority.
Art. 58. If a member does not pay his fees without
authorisation after three months, he will be stricken off the list
of membership of the Party.

Chapter XI.---Association of the Kuomintang Party.
Art. 59. In labour syndicates, clubs, unions, societies,
associations, chambers of commerce, schools, municipal assemblies
district assemblies, provincial assemblies, parliament, in all
secret groups, the members must organize groups in such a manner
as to increase the influence of the Party and increase its
activities.
Art. 60. In this case, the supervision of the special
organizations is vested in the Central Committee.
Art. 61. The Provincial Committee directs the group in the
Provincial Assembly; the Central Committee directs the group in
Parliament; the labour syndicates, clubs etc., come under the
direction of the Local Committee.
Art. 62. In case of a divergence of opinion between the
Assemblies, a special meeting will decide the case. In case of
disagreement, the matter should be referred to the Superior
Committee. Whilst awaiting the decision of the Superior
Committee, the decision of the Local Committee should be
strictly observed.
Art. 63. Members with the permission of the committee
on which they depend may accept official positions. Members of
Parliament belonging to the Party may not accept
official positions or portfolios without first obtaining the
consent of the Central Committee.
Art. 64. The association elects its staff and directors.
Art. 65. All propositions or suggestions must be submitted
and discussed by the Association and the policy to be adopted

第五十四条。凡违反本党律法、不执行本党命令或不认同本党宗旨之党员，将受如下惩处：
其行为将通过本党报刊向全体党员通报。在等待暂时停职或正式除名期间，禁止其担任任何公职。
若同一分部之数名党员犯有相同过错，将按如下方式惩处：
该分部所有成员须重新登记，并决定将其除名或予以宽恕。
该分部可予解散，解散原因将在本党所有报刊上公布。
第五十五条。若某一分部之个别党员或全体党员经监察委员会及地方委员会调查后被认定资格无效或被视为不受欢迎者，可向上级委员会及全国代表大会提出申诉，但在作出裁决之前，其资格视为无效。全国代表大会将决定是否接纳新党员入党，但须经中央委员会批准。在等待中央委员会作出决定期间，大会之决定暂不生效。

第十章——财务。
第五十六条。本党收入由党员缴纳的党费、上级机构筹集的资金以及其他收款组成。
第五十七条。党员每月须缴纳二十仙（cents），但若因病或贫困，经告知地方分部并由该分部上报上级机关批准后，可获准免缴。
第五十八条。若党员未经批准连续三个月未缴纳党费，将从本党党员名册中除名。

第十一章——国民党之组织关联。
第五十九条。在工会、俱乐部、联合会、社团、协会、商会、学校、市议会、区议会、省议会、国会以及所有秘密团体中，党员必须以能够增强本党影响力并扩大本党活动的方式组织小组。
第六十条。在此情况下，对这些特别组织的监督权归属于中央委员会。
第六十一条。省委员会指导省议会中的党团；中央委员会指导国会中的党团；工会、俱乐部等则受地方委员会的指导。
第六十二条。若各分部之间出现意见分歧，将通过特别会议裁定。若仍有异议，应将事项提交上级委员会。在等待上级委员会裁决期间，应严格遵守地方委员会的决定。
第六十三条。党员经其所属委员会许可，可接受公职。属于本党的国会议员，在未事先获得中央委员会同意的情况下，不得接受公职或部长职位。
第六十四条。该协会选举其职员及董事。
第六十五条。所有提案或建议必须提交协会讨论，所采纳之方针

"As a worker who thinks of the problems of Society in terms of human welfare, Dr. Sun believes a Socialistic form of Government would lessen poverty, misery and crime and render life humaner and richer in quality. But as a head of Government, he has not yet envisaged the general adoption of Socialism as an immediate object of policy in Canton or in any other part of Kwangtung."

The above is an extract from an official communication which the Hongkong Telegraph has received from Mr. Eugene Chen in reply to a series of questions which were submitted to him in regard to reports which have been appearing in the vernacular Press to the effect that Dr. Sun Yat-sen has resolved to give the Soviet or Socialistic form of government a trial. In our letter to Mr. Chen we pointed out that these reports have been given considerable prominence and that in the absence of any official denial they were apt to pass as the truth. We therefore sought to ascertain the precise facts on this question and asked for official information on a number of reports. To our enquiries, Mr. Eugene Chen has now replied.

The questions which we addressed to Mr. Eugene Chen, and the answers given by the latter are as follows:—

Question.
Whether Dr. Sun Yat-sen is, or has been, in direct or indirect communication with the Soviet Government?

Answer.
Dr. Sun Yat-sen is and has been in direct communication with the Soviet Government. Historical reasons and the facts of geography compel intercourse between Russia and China. They may be friends or they may be enemies. Under the Tsardom, they were enemies. With Soviet Russia, however, China can be friends. This briefly, is the raison d'etre of Dr. Sun's policy vis-a-vis the Soviet Government—with which, by the way, the British Government is now in direct and official communication.

Question.
Whether there is a Soviet representative at present in Canton, and, if so, the object of his mission?

Answer.
There is a Soviet representative in Canton (he is now on a visit to the North). He has himself stated in the public press that his Mission is similar in aim to that of the Soviet Trade Delegation in London.

Question.
Whether the Soviet Government or its representative has promised to advance to Dr. Sun Yat-sen or the Canton Government any sum of money, or suggested the possibility of such advance being made. If so, what is the amount of such advance and the consideration for the grant thereof?

Answer.
The reply to this question is in the negative.

Question.
Whether any funds whatsoever have been received by Dr. Sun Yat-sen or the Canton Government from Soviet sources?

Answer.
The reply to this question is also in the negative.

Question.
Whether, as a consequence of interviews with the Soviet representative, Dr. Sun Yat-sen has decided (1) to establish a new Military College; (2) to declare the nationalisation of certain, and, if so, what, properties and land?

Answer.
Dr. Sun is now establishing a Military College for the proper training of military officers on modern lines. This is a necessity if Dr. Sun is right in his policy of substituting a small, modern-trained and efficient force for vast numbers of inefficiently trained troops. It was not necessary for the Soviet representative to assist him to realise this obvious point.

Dr. Sun's view on the nationalisation of public utilities and "key" industries are stated at length in his book "The International Development of China", published in Shanghai in 1921 and abroad in 1922 by Messrs. G. P. Putnam's Sons of New York and London. Dr. Sun's views as expressed in his book have undergone no material change or modification as a result of interviews with the Soviet representative.

Question.
Whether Dr. Sun Yat-sen intends to give the Soviet or Socialistic form of government and or "Red" military organisation a trial in Canton or in any other part of Kwangtung?

Answer.
The reply to this question is in the negative. As a worker who thinks of the problems of Society in terms of human welfare, Dr. Sun believes a Socialistic form of government would lessen poverty, misery and crime and render life humaner and richer in quality. But as a head of Government, he has not yet envisaged the general adoption of Socialism as an immediate object of policy in Canton or in any other part of Kwangtung.

There is a report in the enemy press in Hongkong that Communism would be enforced in Canton on the 1st of April. The date is significant! This is a frigid and calculated lie.

《字林西报》，1924年4月6日，星期日

孙中山的观点
社会主义信仰者；无意立即采纳；无苏俄资金

“作为一名从人类福祉角度思考社会问题的工作者，孙博士相信社会主义形式的政府能够减少贫困、苦难和犯罪，使生活更具人性且质量更丰富。但作为政府首脑，他尚未将普遍采纳社会主义作为广州或广东其他任何地区政策的即时目标。”

以上是陈友仁先生回复《香港电讯报》一系列提问的官方通讯摘录，这些提问针对的是中文报刊上出现的报道，称孙中山博士已决心尝试苏维埃或社会主义形式的政府。我们在致陈先生的信中指出，这些报道受到了极大关注，且在缺乏官方否认的情况下，容易被当作事实。因此，我们试图查明关于此问题的确切事实，并就多项报道寻求官方信息。陈友仁先生现已回复我们的询问。

我们向陈友仁先生提出的问题及其回答如下：—

问。
孙中山博士是否曾与苏维埃政府进行过直接或间接的联系？

答。
孙中山博士现在且一直与苏维埃政府保持直接联系。历史原因和地理事实迫使俄国与中国进行交往。他们可能是朋友，也可能是敌人。在沙皇统治下，他们是敌人。然而，对于苏维埃俄国，中国可以成为朋友。简而言之，这就是孙博士对苏维埃政府政策的理由所在——顺便提一句，英国政府目前也正与苏维埃政府进行直接且官方的接触。

问。
目前广州是否有苏维埃代表？如果有，其使命的目标是什么？

答。
广州有一位苏维埃代表（他目前正在北方访问）。他已在公开报刊上声明，其使命的目标与伦敦的苏维埃贸易代表团相似。

问。
苏维埃政府或其代表是否承诺向孙中山博士或广州政府提供任何款项，或暗示可能提供此类款项？如果是，金额是多少，提供该款项的条件是什么？

答。
对此问题的回答是否定的。

问。
孙中山博士或广州政府是否从苏维埃方面收到过任何资金？

答。
对此问题的回答也是否定的。

问。
作为与苏维埃代表会晤的结果，孙中山博士是否决定（1）建立一所新的军事学院；（2）宣布某些财产和土地国有化？如果是，是哪些财产和土地？

答。
孙博士正在建立一所军事学院，以现代方式适当培训军官。如果孙博士以一支小型、受过现代训练且高效的部队取代大量训练低效的部队的政策是正确的，那么此举就是必要的。苏维埃代表没有必要协助他认识到这一显而易见的要点。

孙博士关于公用事业和“关键”工业国有化的观点，在其1921年在上海出版、1922年由纽约和伦敦的G. P. Putnam's Sons公司在海外出版的《中国国际发展》一书中已有详细阐述。孙博士在书中表达的观点并未因与苏维埃代表的会晤而发生实质性改变或修正。

问。
孙中山博士是否打算在广州或广东其他任何地区尝试苏维埃或社会主义形式的政府，或“红色”军事组织？

答。
对此问题的回答是否定的。作为一名从人类福祉角度思考社会问题的工作者，孙博士相信社会主义形式的政府能够减少贫困、苦难和犯罪，使生活更具人性且质量更丰富。但作为政府首脑，他尚未将普遍采纳社会主义作为广州或广东其他任何地区政策的即时目标。

香港敌对报刊中有报道称，共产主义将于4月1日在广州强制实施。这个日期意味深长！这是一个冷酷且蓄意的谎言。

CANTON, TUESDAY, APRIL 1, 1924.
The Kuomintang And Russia.
DRAFT RUSSO-CHINESE AGREEMENT EMBODIES FOREIGN
POLICY OF KUOMINTANG, DECLARES SOVIET
REPRESENTATIVE.
559 u.
7/4/24
The publication of the following official communique
is authorized:—
Dr. Sun Yat-sen has received the following tele-
gram, dated March 23rd, from Mr. Brodin, the Russian
representative at Canton who is presently on a visit to Pe-
king. It may now be stated that, besides discussing with
Mr. Borodin matters directly connected with his Mission, Dr.
Sun has had occasion to communicate to him his views on
the group of major questions awaiting settlement between
China and Russia. These views have since been elaborated
into a body of doctrine relating to China's foreign relations
and incorporated into the official programme of the Kuo-
mintang as defined and settled at the Party Congress
which was recently held at Canton. The telegram reads
as follows:—
"Dr. Sun Yat-sen, Canton: - Prior to the recognition of
Russia by Great Britain and Italy, the Russian Mission in Pe-
king insisted upon the resumption of diplomatic relations first
and conference to be held afterwards for the purpose of settling
all outstanding questions between Russia and China. Following
the recognition of Russia by those two Great Powers, it might
be expected that the Russian Mission would take advantage of
our strengthened position to refuse any concessions to the Peking
Government.
"But this was not the case. On the contrary our Mission
not only did not take advantage of the favourable
situation, but it made a concession of the utmost importance in
that it agreed to settling the principles which are to govern the
future conference and then resume normal diplomatic rela-
tions. Accordingly Mr. Karakhan entered upon long delib-
erations ending in an agreement which was duly signed by
himself and the Chinese plenipotentiary on the 14th inst.
"The Peking Cabinet, however, has refused to accept the
agreement. It has, moreover, repudiated the signature of its
own plenipotentiary.
"What is this agreement which the Peking Cabinet has
refused to accept? The agreement embodies the foreign policy
of the Kuomintang, namely: it repudiates all treaties between
Czarist Russia and China, treaties which deprived China of
her sovereignty; it abolishes the right of extraterritoriality,
consular jurisdiction etc.; it recognizes China's sovereignty
over Mongolia; it establishes signal rights to the management
and operation of the Chinese Eastern Railway until China will
be financially in a position to redeem it completely. It turns
over the Russian share of the Boxer Indemnities to education
in China: it calls for new treaties based upon absolute equality.
"How much blood and treasure would the Chinese people
have to spend before they would be able to get a similar
agreement from the Imperialist Powers? What tremendous
efforts the Nationalist movement, headed by the Kuomintang,
would have to use before it could place China on such a footing
with other Nations as is offered in the agreement?
"Yet the Peking Cabinet has refused to accept it. Why?
It cannot be because it is contrary to the interest of the Chinese
nation. In whose interest, then, was the agreement rejected? It
is quite clear. The agreement is based on the foreign policy of
the Kuomintang as accepted by the Congress of the Party on
the 23rd January last: it is a victory of Nationalism for China.
"Revolutionary Russia has extended a brotherly hand to
her great neighbour struggling for independence. It has offer-
ed a treaty of peace and amity which is bound to be the first
important step on the way to China's endeavour to extricate
herself from the position of a semi-colony. Yet the Peking Ca-
binet has rejected it.
"I am sending to you a copy of the agreement to judge for
yourself whether any Cabinet, aspiring to represent the Nation,
is justified in rejecting it. Your great principle of Nationalism
is in danger of being thwarted by considerations alien to the in-
terest of the Nation. I hope that your great part will take
notice of the seriousness of the situation.
"BORODIN."
