国民党与俄国。
苏联代表宣称：俄中协定草案体现了国民党的外交政策。
559 u.
7/4/24
兹授权发布以下官方公报：—
孙中山博士收到了一封来自布罗丁（Brodin）先生的电报，日期为3月23日。布罗丁先生是俄国驻广州代表，目前正访问北京。现在可以说明的是，除了与鲍罗廷（Borodin）先生讨论与其使命直接相关的事宜外，孙博士还借此机会向他阐述了自己对于待解决的中俄之间一系列重大问题的看法。这些观点随后被 elaborated 为一套关于中国对外关系的学说体系，并被纳入国民党在最近于广州举行的代表大会上所界定和确定的正式纲领中。电文如下：—
“致广州孙中山博士：— 在英国和意大利承认俄国之前，俄国驻北京使团坚持要求先恢复外交关系，然后再举行会议，以解决俄国与中国之间所有悬而未决的问题。在这两个大国承认俄国之后，人们原本预期俄国使团会利用我们地位加强的优势，拒绝向北京政府做出任何让步。
“但事实并非如此。相反，我们的使团不仅没有利用这一有利局势，反而做出了极为重要的让步，即同意确定指导未来会议的原则，然后恢复正常的外交关系。因此，加拉罕（Karakhan）先生开始了漫长的审议，最终达成了一项协议，并于本月14日由他本人和中国全权代表正式签署。
“然而，北京内阁拒绝接受该协议。此外，它还否认了其自身全权代表的签名。
“北京内阁拒绝接受的这项协议究竟是什么？该协议体现了国民党的外交政策，即：废除沙皇俄国与中国之间剥夺中国主权的所有条约；废除领事裁判权、治外法权等；承认中国对蒙古的主权；确立对中国东省铁路管理和运营的显著权利，直至中国在财政上有能力完全赎回该铁路为止。将俄国份额的庚子赔款转用于中国的教育事业；呼吁在绝对平等的基础上订立新条约。
“中国人民需要花费多少鲜血和财富，才能从帝国主义列强那里获得类似的协议？由国民党领导的民族主义运动需要付出多么巨大的努力，才能使中国获得协议中所提供的与其他国家平等的地位？
“然而，北京内阁却拒绝接受它。为什么？这不可能因为它违背了中华民族的利益。那么，是为了谁的利益而拒绝该协议呢？答案很清楚。该协议基于国民党在去年1月23日的党代会上所接受的外交政策：这是中国民族主义的胜利。
“革命俄国已向为其独立而奋斗的伟大邻邦伸出了兄弟般的手。它提供了一份和平友好条约，这必将成为中国努力摆脱半殖民地地位道路上的第一个重要步骤。然而，北京内阁却拒绝了它。
“我随函附上协议副本，供您自行判断，任何声称代表国家的内阁是否有权拒绝它。您伟大的民族主义原则正面临被与国家利益无关的考量所阻碍的危险。我希望贵党能注意到局势的严重性。
鲍罗廷。”

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, MONDAY, APRIL 28, 1924.
DANGEROUS PROPAGANDA
IN NORTHERN CHINA
5594.
2/5/24.
PEKING'S RED CANKER
Some Subterfuges Which Undermine Work
Of Conscientious Chinese
Peking, April 25.
It is only at this late hour that the Chinese authorities are beginning to realize to what a serious extent Bolshevik propaganda has been carried on throughout the country. It is not because of insufficient warning for soon after the arrival of the first Bolshevik representative from the Far Eastern Republic and the establishment of the Rosta Agency, the government was warned time and time again, of the propaganda and the amount of money being spent on it. Those in power at the time refused to pay any attention to the matter, whilst others found a ready source of income by throwing in their lot with the Bolsheviks, who had vast sums of money available for instilling Bolshevik ideas into the Chinese. The original plan of Bolshevizing this country was an extensive one. A large number of Chinese who lived in Russia many years and were in the pay of the Moscow or Chita Government were brought into China and distributed in the most important centres in the north and south. All had been educated in the art of spreading propaganda. Some were of sufficient address, education and intelligence to appeal to professors, other education lists and higher officials. Others were sufficiently young to be able to appeal to students; others were to work on the parliamentarians, while groups were told off to work among the officers, soldiers and labour organizations. The Rosta Agency got to work among the native papers. News sheets were distributed amongst them, ready to be set up, in Chinese. A regular service was given free of charge, and in some instances, control of papers was secured either by subsidy or purchase.
Cunning Camouflage
Pamphlets and hand bills were distributed by hundreds of thousands to workers all over the country, but so efficiently and secretly was the distribution carried out, that it was some time before the government discovered how extensively the programme was being carried out. Some fourteen months ago, the police found large bales of pamphlets in a house in the East City. The confiscated them and when they were opened up it was found that they dealt with such subjects as, "What an Officer should know." What a private soldier should know," what a labourer should know," etc., etc. A little while later a large stack of Bible was discovered in Paotingfu, which instead of containing the scriptures within the covers, were composed of Bolshevik leaflets, and extracts from Carl Marx. Upon these discoveries being made the police for a time became very active, and the Bolshevik representative in Peking at the time was warned that continuation of these propaganda methods would result in the Government demanding his departure. He naturally denied having any knowledge of these activities, and promised the mission would have nothing to do with any form of propaganda. But it went on just the same until to-day the government finds itself faced with a serious problem. There are a number of self admitted Communists in the parliament; a large proportion of the students are out and out Bolsheviks, they having followed the lead of a number of their professors, one of whom was the head of the Peking University and one time Minister of education. Girl students are also among the converts and are likely to play a prominent part in demonstrations in the future. Among the industrial workers, there is also great unrest and the work done among the coolie class is undoubtedly responsible for the present unfriendly feeling shown toward foreigners both in Peking and elsewhere. How much the country will suffer by its having made no serious and organized attempt to close down on the propaganda agencies only the future can show.
A day or two ago a number of Chinese, under Bolshevik leaders protested against the manner in which the soldier who had attacked foreigners on the city wall, was being held by the legation police until the Chinese authorities had assented to bring him to trial, with a British official sitting on the bench, with the object of seeing that justice was done. They violently criticized the British, and subsequently passed the following resolutions: That the British Minister should tender an apology for refusing to surrender the prisoner, which was considered a grave insult to China. (2) That all important places in British concessions in China shall be thrown open to the Chinese. (3) That the British Minister should undertake to offer no similar insult to China in the future. (4) That the government should not defer to the British Minister and inflict undue severe punishment on the cular telegram should be despatched to the country in the name of the parliament and those present at the meeting, outlining the many occasions in which the British have browbeaten the Chinese. (6) That in case the above demands fail of attainment that the Government should put up placards at various important places stating "That Englishmen and dogs are not allowed."
This is typical of the tone of a certain section of the Chinese in North China to-day. That it is to a certain extent childish and ignorant there is no gainsaying, but there is an underlying note of seriousness and danger in it which must be heeded. That the police should make no attempt to prevent a meeting of this nature, shows that either the authorities are afraid of this crowd of truculent politicians, or that no attempt is being made to restrict meetings of this nature. All the papers with but few exceptions captioned the report of the meeting in large type, and some of them strongly commented on the meeting to the detriment of British and foreigners in general. It is not anticipated that this meeting will have much influence on the manner in which the case in question is handled, although it will probably make it a little unpleasant for the Chinese officials who have the case in hand.

《字林西报》，1924年4月28日，星期一。
华北地区的危险宣传
5594.
2/5/24.
北京的红色毒瘤
一些破坏 conscientious 中国人工作的诡计
北京，4月25日。
直到此刻，中国当局才开始意识到布尔什维克宣传在全国范围内进行的严重程度。这并不是因为警告不足，因为在第一位来自远东共和国的布尔什维克代表抵达以及罗斯塔通讯社（Rosta Agency）成立后不久，政府就一次次受到关于宣传及其资金投入的警告。当时的当权者拒绝关注此事，而其他人则通过与布尔什维克同流合污找到了现成的收入来源，后者拥有巨额资金可用于向中国人灌输布尔什维克思想。将该国布尔什维克化的原始计划规模庞大。大量在中国居住多年、受莫斯科或赤塔（Chita）政府雇佣的中国人被带入中国，并分布在南北最重要的中心。所有人都受过传播宣传的艺术教育。有些人具备足够的风度、教育和智慧，以吸引教授、其他教育工作者和高级官员；有些人足够年轻，能够吸引学生；另一些人则致力于影响议员，同时还有小组被指派在军官、士兵和劳工组织中开展工作。罗斯塔通讯社开始在本地报纸中开展工作。中文排版的新闻稿被分发给它们，随时可供排版。定期免费提供服务，在某些情况下，通过补贴或购买获得了报纸的控制权。
巧妙的伪装
数以十万计的小册子和传单被分发给全国各地的工人，但由于分发工作执行得如此高效和秘密，政府过了一段时间才发现该计划实施的广泛程度。大约十四个月前，警察在东城的的一所房子里发现了大批小册子。他们没收了这些小册子，打开后发现其内容涉及“军官应知事项”、“普通士兵应知事项”、“劳工应知事项”等等。不久之后，在保定府发现了一大批《圣经》，其封面内包含的不是经文，而是布尔什维克传单和卡尔·马克思的摘录。在这些发现之后，警方一度变得非常活跃，当时在北京的布尔什维克代表受到警告，如果继续这些宣传手段，政府将要求他离境。他自然否认知晓这些活动，并承诺使团不会参与任何形式的宣传。但宣传工作依然如故，直到今天，政府发现自己面临着一个严重的问题。议会中有一些自认的共产主义者；很大一部分学生是彻底的布尔什维克，他们追随了一些教授的引导，其中一位曾是北京大学校长和前教育总长。女学生中也出现了皈依者，她们很可能在未来的示威活动中发挥突出作用。在产业工人中，也存在极大的不安，而在苦力阶层中进行的工作无疑导致了目前在北京及其他地方表现出的对外国人的不友好情绪。该国因未认真和有组织地试图关闭宣传机构而将遭受多大损失，只有未来才能显示。
一两天前，一些中国人在布尔什维克领导人的带领下，抗议使馆警察拘押一名在城墙上袭击外国人的士兵的方式，直到中国当局同意将其交付审判，并由一名英国官员坐堂审案，以确保公正执行。他们猛烈批评英国人，随后通过了以下决议：(1) 英国公使应就拒绝移交囚犯一事道歉，这被视为对中国的严重侮辱。(2) 英国在华租界的所有重要场所应向中国人开放。(3) 英国公使应承诺今后不再对中国施加类似侮辱。(4) 政府不应顺从英国公使，并对……施加不当的严厉惩罚（原文此处似乎有缺漏或乱码，结合上下文推测可能指相关人员）……应以议会及与会者的名义向全国发出通电，概述英国人多次欺压中国人的情况。(6) 如果上述要求未能实现，政府应在各个重要地点张贴标语，写明“英人与狗不得入内”。
这就是当今华北地区部分中国人语调的典型代表。不可否认，这在一定程度上显得幼稚和无知，但其中蕴含着必须予以重视的严肃性和危险性基调。警方未试图阻止此类集会，表明当局要么害怕这群好斗的政治家，要么并未试图限制此类集会。除少数例外，所有报纸都以大号字体刊登了会议报道，其中一些报纸对会议进行了强烈评论，损害了英国人及一般外国人的形象。预计此次会议不会对处理本案的方式产生太大影响，尽管这可能会让负责此案的中国官员感到些许不快。
